text:
Maya Chen: Morning — quick async standup. What I did / blockers / today
- Did: landed kernel slot allocator fix + small change to the batching heuristics to avoid micro-batches at tail.
- Blocker: seeing a KV cold-start spike p95 on canary (shard-7) after the allocator change; likely warmup ordering.
- Today: iterate on kv preheat script, run perf sweep across canary nodes, and coordinate a small canary rollout. Pinging @Sam for trace pulls.

Sam Patel: On it. I grabbed traces for the two affected windows and uploaded to the trace bucket: https://go/retrace/canary-shard7-2026-03-18.
Quick note: noticed GC-ish GPU memory churn around 10:12 UTC on gpu-node-12, might correlate with concurrent slot reclamation.

Devon Li: I ran a microbench locally to reproduce warmup tail. Command I used:
```bash
./bench --mode=kv-warm --shard 7 --iters 500 --seq-len 512
```
Sample output (trimmed):
```
[INFO] iter=100 p95=42.3ms p99=210.1ms kv_miss=0.13
[INFO] iter=300 p95=47.8ms p99=325.7ms kv_miss=0.27 -> spike after slot reclaim
```
Hypothesis: prefetch scheduling sometimes races with slot allocation causing more cache misses for first few batches.

Riley Torres: I'll queue a canary with preheat=15s and a slightly larger initial batcher window to help warm the KV. Can someone +1 the rollout? ops-bot will need approval annotation.

Maya Chen: @Riley go ahead. @ops-bot do we have capacity to add the extra 2 GPU slots for a 30min canary? Also note fallback policy is configured to model-quant-lite if latency crosses threshold.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary started: canary-2026-03-18-09; reserved 2 GPU slots on rg-4; preheat=15s; fallback=model-quant-lite. Link: https://go/deploys/canary-2026-03-18-09

Sam Patel: If p95 remains high after preheat, try lowering kv.cap to 0.75 in runtime config to reduce eviction churn (will trade some memory headroom). Also capture `kv.hit_rate` and `evict_ops` counters.

Devon Li: Small batching tweak suggestion: reduce `batcher.max_wait_ms` from 8 -> 6 for low-qps tenants to cut tail latency on micro-queries. I'll open a PR with metrics gathered.

Maya Chen: Ack, thanks. I'll run the perf sweep (canary + control) and post diffs by EOD. If anyone can review PR #4212 (batcher wait reduction + allocator fix) that would speed rollout.

Riley Torres: Reviewing #4212 now — found one doc nit on config comments, otherwise looks good.

Sam Patel: :thumbsup: will review traces after the canary runs finish.

Maya Chen: Thanks all. Blocking action items: Devon opens PR (in flight), Riley merges canary results into the perf dashboard, Sam posts traces + a short note if GPU churn persists. I'll follow up with numbers later today.

(ops-bot reaction: :rocket:)
